entries.title: Friend check-in missing from browser notification inbox
entries.summary: Jesse reported accepting a friendship, enabling friend check-in alerts, then checking in without a notification appearing in the recipient inbox. He explicitly distinguished the persistent inbox from device push delivery. This observation is recorded as owner evidence.
entries.detail: The current chat does not identify the exact accounts or event row. Do not erase this result or infer the owner never tested it. The source/deployed-code investigation below establishes the manual-path gap without claiming the exact user event was queried.

entries.title: Live manual Check In path does not create a friend-inbox row
entries.summary: Read-only inspection of LocalCheckProd confirmed public.check_in inserts check_ins, whose triggers update activity/metrics, broadcast invalidations and schedule checkout; none creates a friend notification. Friend rows are created by auto-check-in posting. The inbox itself reads own persisted notifications newest first, limited to 50.
entries.current_state: Inbox gap confirmed in deployed functions; no database or app fix deployed. Shared log publication is being finished. Product implementation remains unassigned.
entries.detail: Verified explicit project qkrnmyexzvaxiqfxwwfb / LocalCheckProd before querying catalog definitions. Inspected public.check_in, private.post_auto_check_in, create_notification, check_ins triggers and their functions, and activity_events trigger. Auto friend eligibility: sender share_auto_check_ins on, profile not Private, accepted friendship, receiver notify_friend_check_ins on, no blocks, hidden-account recipient eligibility, no same sender/recipient friend alert in prior two hours. Push disabled/no token does not prevent inbox insertion. No private user row, account credential or real test event was mutated. Separate source issue: fetchNotifications turns read errors into an empty array, so the screen can show an empty state after a failed fetch; that was not established as the cause of Jesse’s event.

entries.title: Inbox logging is independent of phone push capability
entries.summary: Jesse clarified that the browser-disabled Push notifications toggle must not prevent notification-inbox logging. Keep phone-push behavior separate; the inbox should retain eligible user notifications even without device push. A test account was supplied privately; its credentials are excluded from the shared record.
entries.detail: Read-only inspection of the supplied BASE observer at this snapshot: receive-friend-alert preference on, global push off, zero inbox rows and zero accepted friendships. This is the supplied observer baseline, not a claim about the identities or friendship involved in Jesse’s earlier reported test. No account state changed. The confirmed deployed manual-notification gap remains.
